headline: Resilience is recovering from setbacks—the ability to fall, get up, and continue forward
universal_truth: Failure is information, not identity; setbacks teach more than successes
fun_facts: Post-traumatic growth is real—many people report positive life changes after hardship
Resilient people often have strong social connections that support them through difficulty
Reframing setbacks as challenges rather than threats activates different brain regions
discussion_questions: What setback taught you the most?
What helps you recover when things go wrong?
How has difficulty changed you for the better?

hook.script: Everyone fails. Everyone faces setbacks. The difference isn't who falls—it's who gets back up. Resilience isn't avoiding difficulty; it's recovering from it. And like a muscle, it can be strengthened.

cliff.script: Some people seem to bounce back from anything while others crumble under pressure. Is resilience something you're born with, or something you can develop?

options.text: Resilience is built through experience, perspective, and relationships—it's developed, not innate
options.response: Yes. Resilience grows through facing difficulty, developing coping strategies, and building support networks. Each setback you survive makes the next one easier.

options.text: Some people are naturally tougher and more resilient
options.response: Temperament varies, but resilience is primarily learned...

fact1.title: Post-Traumatic Growth
fact1.script: Many people emerge from hardship stronger than before—this is 'post-traumatic growth.' Difficulty can reveal hidden strength, clarify priorities, and deepen relationships. What doesn't kill you can literally make you stronger.

fact2.title: Reframing
fact2.script: How you interpret setbacks matters enormously. Viewing them as temporary, specific, and external ('this project failed') versus permanent, global, and personal ('I'm a failure') determines how fast you recover.

fact3.title: Support Systems
fact3.script: Resilience isn't solo—it's social. People with strong support networks recover faster. Having someone to talk to, lean on, and gain perspective from multiplies your ability to bounce back. Build your network before you need it.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Failure is information, not identity. Resilience teaches that setbacks teach more than successes. The goal isn't to never fall—it's to always get up.

outro.script: That's Day 190—190 days of learning! Tomorrow, we'll explore trusting yourself—confidence. Until then, remember a setback that ultimately made you stronger.

growTrack.title: Setback Story - Find the Gift
growTrack.activity: Think of a past setback or failure. How did you grow from it? What did it teach you? How are you different because of it? Reframing past difficulties as teachers builds resilience for future ones.
